exam.name: Implementing End-to-End Security Controls for Cloud and AI Workloads
exam.certification: Microsoft Certified: Cloud and AI Security Engineer Associate (beta)
exam.retirementDate: Not yet announced (exam currently in beta)

objectives.title: Secure access with Microsoft Entra ID
objectives.description: Privileged Identity Management (eligible vs active, activation policies), Conditional Access (assignments, grant/session controls, report-only), and authentication methods (MFA, passwordless, phishing-resistant methods, licensing).
officialSkills: Configure Privileged Identity Management (PIM) eligible assignments and activation policies for Entra and Azure resource roles
Design and implement Conditional Access policies (assignments, grant controls, session controls, authentication strength)
Configure authentication methods, passwordless options, and the Authentication methods policy
Distinguish Entra ID P1 vs P2 licensing requirements for CA, Identity Protection, and PIM
Configure break-glass accounts excluded from Conditional Access and PIM

objectives.title: Application identity, OAuth consent & managed identities
objectives.description: App registration vs enterprise application (service principal), delegated vs application OAuth permissions and consent, user/admin consent settings, and system-assigned vs user-assigned managed identities.
officialSkills: Differentiate app registrations from enterprise applications (service principals)
Configure delegated vs application OAuth permissions and the consent workflow
Restrict user consent and configure the admin consent request workflow
Choose between system-assigned and user-assigned managed identities
Prefer managed identity over service principal with certificate or client secret

objectives.title: Secure secrets & keys with Azure Key Vault
objectives.description: Key Vault object types (keys, secrets, certificates), Azure RBAC vs vault access policy authorization models, network restriction and private endpoints, and Defender for Key Vault vs Defender CSPM secret scanning.
officialSkills: Deploy and harden a Key Vault (RBAC authorization, soft-delete, purge protection, network restriction)
Choose between Azure RBAC and legacy vault access policy authorization models
Grant a managed identity data-plane access to secrets via RBAC roles
Distinguish Defender for Key Vault (runtime threat detection) from Defender CSPM secret scanning (posture)
Use customer-managed keys (CMK) and Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) for encryption at rest

objectives.title: Governance: Azure Policy, RBAC, resource locks, backup & IaC
objectives.description: Azure Policy effects (Audit, Deny, DeployIfNotExists, Modify, AuditIfNotExists), Azure RBAC vs Microsoft Entra roles, resource locks, Azure Backup hardening (soft delete, immutable vaults, Multi-User Authorization), regulatory compliance, and Infrastructure as Code security.
officialSkills: Assign built-in and custom Azure Policy definitions and initiatives with the correct effect
Apply least-privilege Azure RBAC role assignments and distinguish them from Microsoft Entra directory roles
Configure resource locks (CanNotDelete, ReadOnly) and Azure Backup hardening (soft delete, immutable vaults, MUA)
Map an environment to regulatory compliance standards in Defender for Cloud
Secure Infrastructure as Code (Bicep/ARM/Terraform) with pre-deployment scanning and DevOps security

objectives.title: Security for storage accounts
objectives.description: Storage account hardening (secure transfer, minimum TLS, public blob access, Shared Key authorization), SAS types and stored access policies, network restriction (service endpoint vs private endpoint), and Defender for Storage.
officialSkills: Harden a storage account: require secure transfer, minimum TLS 1.2, disable public blob access and Shared Key authorization
Choose the appropriate SAS type (account, service, user delegation) and apply stored access policies
Restrict storage network access using service endpoints vs private endpoints
Enable Microsoft Defender for Storage (malware scanning, sensitive data threat detection)
Apply customer-managed keys and infrastructure encryption for storage accounts

objectives.title: Security for databases (Azure SQL)
objectives.description: Azure SQL authentication (Microsoft Entra auth, Entra-only auth), network restriction (firewall rules, private endpoint), Transparent Data Encryption vs Always Encrypted vs Dynamic Data Masking, Row-Level Security, and SQL Auditing vs Defender for Databases.
officialSkills: Configure Microsoft Entra authentication and Entra-only auth for Azure SQL
Restrict Azure SQL network access with firewall rules and private endpoints
Differentiate TDE (at rest), Always Encrypted (in use), and Dynamic Data Masking (cosmetic)
Configure Row-Level Security and Vulnerability Assessment baselines
Distinguish SQL Auditing (logging) from Microsoft Defender for Databases (threat alerts)

objectives.title: Security for Azure network services
objectives.description: NSGs and Application Security Groups, Azure Firewall vs WAF vs DDoS Protection, Private Link and private endpoints, and connectivity at scale (Virtual WAN, Azure Virtual Network Manager security admin rules, VPN, Entra Private Access).
officialSkills: Design NSG rules and use Application Security Groups for role-based, IP-independent segmentation
Select the correct control among NSG, Azure Firewall, WAF, and DDoS Protection for a given threat layer
Deploy Private Link / private endpoints and resolve the private-DNS-zone requirement
Use Azure Virtual Network Manager security admin rules to enforce estate-wide controls that override NSGs
Harden VPN connectivity and evaluate Microsoft Entra Private Access (Global Secure Access) as a VPN alternative

objectives.title: Security for AI (Copilot, Foundry, Entra Agent ID, Purview DSPM for AI)
objectives.description: AI-specific risks (prompt injection, oversharing, autonomous agents), Purview DSPM for AI (data risk assessment, one-click policies), Microsoft Entra Agent ID (agent identity, Conditional Access for agents), and threat/posture (Defender for AI Services, Microsoft Foundry guardrails, AI gateway via APIM).
officialSkills: Run a Purview DSPM for AI data risk assessment to find SharePoint/OneDrive oversharing before Copilot rollout
Configure Microsoft Entra Agent ID identities and Conditional Access policies scoped to agent risk
Enable Microsoft Defender for AI Services and interpret its alert types (jailbreak, data leakage, wallet attack)
Apply Microsoft Foundry guardrails (Prompt Shields, content filters, blocklists, MCP allowed-tools list)
Deploy Azure API Management as an AI gateway (Entra auth, token rate-limiting, centralized logging)

objectives.title: Security for servers & virtual machines
objectives.description: VM encryption options (encryption at host, Azure Disk Encryption, CMK), Azure Bastion vs Just-In-Time VM access, Trusted launch, Defender for Servers (Plan 1 vs Plan 2), Azure Arc, and agentless scanning.
officialSkills: Choose between encryption at host, Azure Disk Encryption, and server-side CMK encryption for VM disks
Combine Azure Bastion and Just-In-Time VM access to eliminate standing exposure of management ports
Enable Trusted launch (Secure Boot + vTPM) to defend against rootkits and boot-kits
Distinguish Defender for Servers Plan 1 (EDR only) from Plan 2 (adds MDVM, agentless scanning, JIT, FIM)
Onboard non-Azure servers with Azure Arc for unified governance and Defender coverage

objectives.title: Security for application platform services
objectives.description: Container security (Defender for Containers, AKS hardening, ACR hardening), App Service/Functions/Logic Apps authentication and network controls, Web Application Firewall placement (Application Gateway vs Front Door), and API Management protection.
officialSkills: Harden Azure Kubernetes Service (Entra + Kubernetes RBAC, private clusters, network policies, workload identity)
Harden Azure Container Registry (disable admin user, Entra/RBAC, private endpoint, content trust)
Configure App Service/Functions/Logic Apps authentication, network restrictions, and managed identity access
Place Web Application Firewall correctly on Application Gateway (regional) vs Front Door (global)
Protect back-end APIs with Azure API Management (Entra/OAuth validation, rate-limit/quota policies)

objectives.title: Manage posture with Microsoft Defender for Cloud
objectives.description: Defender for Cloud as a CNAPP (CSPM + CWP), Secure Score, free vs paid Defender CSPM tiers (attack path analysis, cloud security explorer, EASM), regulatory compliance dashboard, workload protection plans, and multicloud connectors (AWS/GCP).
officialSkills: Interpret Secure Score and prioritize security recommendations by impact
Distinguish free foundational CSPM from paid Defender CSPM features (attack path analysis, cloud security explorer, EASM)
Map an environment to a regulatory compliance standard and track pass/fail evidence
Enable and scope per-resource Defender workload protection plans
Connect AWS and GCP accounts to Defender for Cloud using native, secret-free federation
Differentiate Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management (inward CVE detection) from External Attack Surface Management (outward asset discovery)

objectives.title: Activity & event collection in Microsoft Sentinel
objectives.description: Sentinel as SIEM+SOAR on a Log Analytics workspace, Sentinel RBAC roles, Content hub data connectors (native, AMA/DCR, CEF/Syslog), analytics rules vs incidents vs automation rules vs playbooks, and retention tiers with the unified Defender portal.
officialSkills: Onboard Microsoft Sentinel onto a Log Analytics workspace and assign the correct Sentinel role (Reader/Responder/Contributor)
Configure data connectors for Microsoft cloud sources, Windows Security events (AMA + DCR), and CEF/Syslog appliances
Author analytics rules and distinguish alerts, incidents, automation rules, and playbooks
Choose the correct log retention tier (interactive analytics vs long-term/archive) for a given cost/query requirement
Use the unified Microsoft Defender portal for cross-Sentinel/XDR advanced hunting

objectives.title: Microsoft Security Copilot
objectives.description: Security Copilot standalone vs embedded modes, Security Compute Units (SCU) capacity, owner vs contributor roles, and plugins/promptbooks/agents extending Copilot's reach across Defender, Sentinel, Entra, Intune, and Purview.
officialSkills: Provision Security Copilot capacity (SCUs) and configure the default environment
Assign owner vs contributor roles for Security Copilot administration and usage
Enable and troubleshoot plugins that connect Copilot to Defender, Sentinel, Entra, and Purview
Distinguish standalone Security Copilot sessions from embedded experiences inside other portals
Use promptbooks and autonomous agents for repeatable security investigations
